key_insight: The LLM ranked solid-state synthesis recipes mainly by thermal features, with reaction chemistry modulating its judgments.
engineering_relevance: LLMs may provide a thermally informed prior for prioritizing synthesis recipes, but experimental validation remains essential.
method: Run 240 synthesis experiments across eight known and unknown inorganic oxide targets.
Use GPT-5.6-Sol to compare recipe pairs, then aggregate preferences with a regularized Bradley–Terry model.
Evaluate rankings against X-ray diffraction purity measurements and selectively withhold recipe information.
evidence_signal: Pairwise accuracy was 0.72 overall; on six thermally driven targets, accuracy was 0.68 without chemical identity versus 0.56 without temperature.
watch_item: Results concern ranking fixed recipe banks for eight oxides, not generating successful recipes or demonstrating broad synthesis generalization.
paper_title: What Do LLMs Use to Judge Synthesis Recipes? An Experimental Analysis on 240 Solid-State Syntheses
